parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State the relationship between gravitational potential and gravitational field strength.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
A moon of mass *M* and radius *R* orbits a planet of mass 3*M* and radius 2*R*. At a particular time, the distance between their centres is *D*, as shown in Fig. 2.1.

[[fig:f1]]

Point P is a point along the line between the centres of the planet and the moon, at a variable distance *x* from the centre of the planet.

The variation with *x* of the gravitational potential *ϕ* at point P, for points between the planet and the moon, is shown in Fig. 2.2.

[[fig:f2]]
parts.text: Explain why *ϕ* is negative throughout the entire range *x* = 2*R* to *x* = *D* − *R*.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
One of the features of Fig. 2.2 is that *ϕ* is negative throughout.

Describe two other features of Fig. 2.2.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
On Fig. 2.3, sketch the variation with *x* of the gravitational field strength *g* at point P between *x* = 2*R* and *x* = *D* − *R*.

[[fig:f3]]

figures.caption: Fig. 2.1
figures.alt: Diagram of a planet and a moon on a line, with their centres separated by distance D, and point P at distance x from the planet's centre.

figures.caption: Fig. 2.2
figures.alt: Graph of gravitational potential ϕ against distance x, with a curve below the horizontal axis between 2R and D − R.

figures.caption: Fig. 2.3
figures.alt: Blank grid with axes for gravitational field strength g against distance x, marked at 2R and D − R.
